title: Creation of ASEAN haze pollution center pushed
summary: Southeast Asian leaders urged ASEAN member-states to prioritize the ratification of an agreement establishing the ASEAN Coordinating Center for Transboundary Haze Pollution Control to make the center…

blocks.text: A thick haze shrouds Metro Manila due to smoke from ongoing forest fires in Kalimantan, Indonesia, in this photo taken from a building in Manila on September 1, 2026

MANILA, Philippines — Southeast Asian leaders urged ASEAN member-states to prioritize the ratification of an agreement establishing the ASEAN Coordinating Center for Transboundary Haze Pollution Control (ACCTHPC) to make the center operational.
Foreign Affairs Secretary Ma. Theresa Lazaro said there were discussions on transboundary haze.
“Indonesia was very frank and candid in expressing the efforts that they have been exerting in addressing the forest fires in Indonesia,” Lazaro said at a press conference.
She stated there were also discussions on the strengthening of law enforcement against companies and people with disruptive practices that have caused the haze from forest fires in Indonesia.
Lazaro said the leaders encouraged ASEAN member-states to prioritize the ratification of the ACCTHPC.
The Indonesian Foreign Ministry said the agreement establishing the ASEAN haze center would take effect once six ASEAN member-states submitted their instruments of ratification.
